en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Protruding the Tongue.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks ate with their tongues protruding...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not eat with my tongue protruding.
One must not eat with one's tongue protruding."
Whoever, out of disrespect, eats with the tongue protruding, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional … [and so forth] …
"For one who is a first offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
